```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Avachat_2025_vancomycin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Avachat_2025_vancomycin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2025.1506793>
* Open-access copy: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11897554/>

# Population

Avachat 2025 is a retrospective analysis of therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM)
data from **90 critically ill patients** treated with intravenous vancomycin at
Kaohsiung Veterans General Hospital, Taiwan, between 2014 and 2016 (Table 1).
Ninety percent were children: median age 3.7 years (range 0.1 to 36.6) and
median weight 12.6 kg (range 0.7 to 93). There were 47 males and 43 females.
Median eGFR (bedside Schwartz) was 70.4 (range 2.4 to 150.6); one patient was on
regular haemodialysis and one on CRRT. Twelve patients (13.3%) were on
extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and 33 (36.7%) had surgery.

The authors grouped the nine admission diagnoses by the severity of the
infection for which vancomycin was given: **severe** = pneumonia (20),
bacteremia (6), osteomyelitis (7), meningitis (4) and deep tissue infection (1),
38 patients; **mild** = cellulitis (6), surgical prevention (35), neutropenic
fever (4) and others (7), 52 patients. The 263 concentrations were mostly
troughs (drawn within 30 min before a dose), with some peaks (> 1 h after the
end of infusion). The model was fitted in Phoenix NLME 8.2 with FOCE-ELS.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Avachat_2025_vancomycin")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` = log(1.03) | 1.03 L/h | Table 4, `tvCL (L/h)` (SE 0.099, 95% CI 0.84-1.23) |
| `lvc` = log(11.61) | 11.61 L | Table 4, `tvV (L)` (SE 1.22, 95% CI 9.2-14.03) |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.75 (fixed) | Table 4, `dCldWT (fixed)`; Section 2.2 |
| `e_wt_vc` | 1 (fixed) | Table 4, `dVdWT (fixed)`; Section 2.2 |
| `e_ecmo_status_cl` | -0.81 | Table 4, `dCldECMO` (SE 0.17, 95% CI -1.14 to -0.47) |
| `e_infect_mild_cl` | -0.49 | Table 4, `dCldDiag` (SE 0.18, 95% CI -0.84 to -0.14) |
| `etalcl` | 0.26 (variance) | Table 4, `eta Cl` (SE 0.08, shrinkage 0.27) |
| `etalvc` | 0.24 (variance) | Table 4, `eta V` (SE 0.07, shrinkage 0.52) |
| `propSd` | 0.44 | Table 4, `Stdev0` (SE 0.03); Section 3.2 proportional error |
| Reference weight 12.6 kg | n/a | Section 3.3 equations (`WT/median(WT)`) and the following paragraph; Table 1 median |
| `cl` equation | n/a | Section 3.3, first final-model equation |
| `vc` equation | n/a | Section 3.3, second final-model equation |
| One compartment, first-order elimination | n/a | Section 3.2 |

# Verification against the published worked example

Table 3 of the paper substitutes the final estimates into the clearance equation
for a 12.6 kg patient with no random effect. The packaged model, solved with the
random effects removed, must reproduce it.

```{r table3}
mod <- readModelDb("Avachat_2025_vancomycin")

tab3 <- tibble::tibble(
  id              = 1:4,
  group           = c("No ECMO, severe infection", "ECMO, severe infection",
                      "No ECMO, mild infection", "ECMO, mild infection"),
  ECMO_STATUS     = c(0, 1, 0, 1),
  DIS_INFECT_MILD = c(0, 0, 1, 1),
  # Table 3 'Clearance value (L/h)'; the paper does not tabulate the
  # combined ECMO + mild group.
  cl_paper        = c(1.03, 0.48, 0.63, NA),
  pct_paper       = c(NA, 56, 39, NA)
)

typ_ev <- tab3 |>
  select(id, ECMO_STATUS, DIS_INFECT_MILD) |>
  mutate(WT = 12.6) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, 1)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = NA_real_)

typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typ_ev) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(cl = first(cl), vc = first(vc), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(tab3, by = "id") |>
  mutate(pct_reduction = 100 * (1 - cl / cl[1]))

typ |>
  select(group, cl, cl_paper, pct_reduction, pct_paper, vc) |>
  rename(
    "Group"                       = group,
    "CL, model (L/h)"             = cl,
    "CL, Table 3 (L/h)"           = cl_paper,
    "CL reduction, model (%)"     = pct_reduction,
    "CL reduction, paper (%)"     = pct_paper,
    "V, model (L)"                = vc
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits  = 3,
    caption = "Typical clearance at the 12.6 kg reference weight, against Avachat 2025 Table 3."
  )

# Deterministic arithmetic: no random effects on either side.
stopifnot(
  abs(typ$cl[1] - 1.03) < 1e-8,
  abs(typ$vc[1] - 11.61) < 1e-8,
  abs(typ$cl[3] - 0.63) < 0.005,
  abs(typ$pct_reduction[2] - 56) < 1,
  abs(typ$pct_reduction[3] - 39) < 1
)
```

The model reproduces the reference clearance, the mild-infection clearance
(0.631 L/h against the printed 0.63) and both percentage reductions (55.5% and
38.7%, printed as about 56% and 39%). Table 3 and the Results text print the ECMO
clearance as 0.48 L/h, but the substitution the table itself writes out,
`1.03 * 1^0.75 * exp(-0.81)`, evaluates to 0.458 L/h; the printed 0.48 does not
follow from the printed estimates, while the printed 56% reduction does. The
model uses the Table 4 estimate of -0.81.

Typical elimination half-life for a 12.6 kg patient with a severe infection and
no ECMO is `log(2) * 11.61 / 1.03` = `r round(log(2) * 11.61 / 1.03, 1)` h.

# Virtual cohort

Individual data are not published. The cohort below draws body weight from a
log-normal distribution with the cohort median of 12.6 kg, truncated to the
observed 0.7 to 93 kg range. The paper reports no dosing regimen (only that
infusion rates ranged from 8 to 1500 mg/h), so every subject receives
**15 mg/kg every 6 h as a 1-h infusion** (60 mg/kg/day), a common paediatric
starting regimen. This is an assumption of the vignette.

Each of the four covariate groups (ECMO yes/no by severe/mild infection) gets
100 subjects with identical weight draws, so the groups differ only by the
covariate effects and the random effects. Concentrations are simulated at
steady state with `ss = 1`, over one dosing interval.

```{r cohort}
# set.seed() fixes the weight draws. rxode2's own random-effect draws are not
# reproducible across rxode2 builds or thread counts, so the assertions below
# compare each subject with itself or with closed forms.
set.seed(20251306)

n_per_group <- 100L
tau         <- 6
infusion_h  <- 1

draw_trunc_lnorm <- function(n, median_value, sdlog, lower, upper) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    cand <- stats::rlnorm(n * 3L, log(median_value), sdlog)
    out <- c(out, cand[cand >= lower & cand <= upper])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

weights <- draw_trunc_lnorm(n_per_group, 12.6, 1.1, 0.7, 93)

groups <- tab3 |>
  select(group, ECMO_STATUS, DIS_INFECT_MILD) |>
  mutate(group_index = seq_len(n()))

subjects <- groups |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(subject = seq_len(n_per_group)) |>
  mutate(
    id  = (group_index - 1L) * n_per_group + subject,
    WT  = weights[subject],
    amt = 15 * WT
  )

doses <- subjects |>
  mutate(
    time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "central",
    rate = amt / infusion_h, ss = 1L, ii = tau
  )

# Observation rows reference the ODE state, never the observable Cc.
obs <- subjects |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = seq(0, tau, by = 0.05)) |>
  mutate(
    evid = 0L, cmt = "central", amt = NA_real_,
    rate = NA_real_, ss = NA_integer_, ii = NA_real_
  )

events <- bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, rate, ss, ii, WT, ECMO_STATUS,
         DIS_INFECT_MILD, group)

stopifnot(length(unique(events$id)) == 4L * n_per_group)

cat(sprintf(
  "Weights: median %.1f kg (range %.1f-%.1f)\n",
  median(weights), min(weights), max(weights)
))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("group", "WT")) |>
  as.data.frame()

stopifnot(all(c("Cc", "cl", "vc") %in% names(sim)))
```

# Steady-state profiles by covariate group

Figure 3 of the paper is a visual predictive check against time since the
first dose (up to about 8000 h) for the observed regimens, which are not
published, so it cannot be redrawn. The plot below shows the steady-state
interval for the assumed regimen in each covariate group, on the same
logarithmic concentration axis.

```{r profiles, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  group_by(group, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    Q50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)",
    y = "Vancomycin concentration (mg/L)",
    caption = "15 mg/kg q6h, 1-h infusion. Median and 5th-95th percentile of individual predictions, 100 subjects per group."
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, group)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
  sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id,
  concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h"
)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, group)

dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id,
  doseu = "mg"
)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start   = 0,
  end     = tau,
  auclast = TRUE,
  cmax    = TRUE,
  cmin    = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  select(group, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

nca_wide |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    cmax    = median(cmax),
    cmin    = median(cmin),
    auclast = median(auclast),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(
    "Group"                      = group,
    "Median Cmax,ss (mg/L)"      = cmax,
    "Median Cmin,ss (mg/L)"      = cmin,
    "Median AUC0-6,ss (mg*h/L)"  = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Steady-state NCA by covariate group, 15 mg/kg q6h.")
```

## Mass balance: steady-state AUC over one interval equals Dose/CL

For a linear model the steady-state AUC over one dosing interval equals
`Dose / CL` for each subject. Both sides use the same simulated individual
clearance, so the only difference is trapezoidal error on the 0.05 h grid and a
tight bound is right.

```{r mass-balance}
mb <- nca_wide |>
  left_join(
    sim |> group_by(id) |> summarise(cl = first(cl), WT = first(WT), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "id"
  ) |>
  mutate(ratio = auclast / (15 * WT / cl))

tibble(
  Subjects          = nrow(mb),
  `Max |ratio - 1|` = max(abs(mb$ratio - 1))
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 6, caption = "PKNCA AUC0-tau at steady state against Dose/CL.")

stopifnot(nrow(mb) == 4L * n_per_group, max(abs(mb$ratio - 1)) < 1e-3)
```

## Group contrasts

The median steady-state AUC ratio between groups is the clearance ratio:
exp(-0.81) = 0.445 for ECMO and exp(-0.49) = 0.613 for a mild infection, so
AUC rises 2.25-fold on ECMO and 1.63-fold for a mild infection. Because the
groups share weight draws but not random effects, the comparison is on medians.

```{r contrasts}
auc_med <- nca_wide |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(auc = median(auclast), .groups = "drop")

ref_auc <- auc_med$auc[auc_med$group == "No ECMO, severe infection"]

contrast <- auc_med |>
  mutate(
    ratio_sim      = auc / ref_auc,
    ratio_expected = c(
      "No ECMO, severe infection" = 1,
      "ECMO, severe infection"    = exp(0.81),
      "No ECMO, mild infection"   = exp(0.49),
      "ECMO, mild infection"      = exp(0.81 + 0.49)
    )[group],
    pct_diff = 100 * (ratio_sim / ratio_expected - 1)
  )

contrast |>
  rename(
    "Group"                       = group,
    "Median AUC0-6,ss (mg*h/L)"   = auc,
    "AUC ratio, simulated"        = ratio_sim,
    "AUC ratio, 1/CL multiplier"  = ratio_expected,
    "% difference"                = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median steady-state AUC relative to the reference group.")

# Centre-based: the group medians are drawn from 100 subjects each with
# omega^2(CL) = 0.26, so the median ratio scatters by roughly 10-15%. A
# mis-signed or mis-transcribed coefficient moves a ratio by 50% or more.
stopifnot(all(abs(contrast$pct_diff) < 30))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Omega scale.** Table 4 lists `eta Cl` = 0.26 and `eta V` = 0.24 without
  stating whether these are variances or standard deviations. Phoenix NLME
  reports the Omega matrix as variances, so they are used as variances
  (lognormal CV about 54% and 52%). The paper's `%CV` column beside them is the
  relative standard error of the estimate (0.08 / 0.26 = 30.7%), not the
  between-subject CV.
* **Residual error.** Section 3.2 selects a proportional error model and
  Section 5 describes "a relatively high residual error of 44%"; Table 4's
  `Stdev0` = 0.44 is therefore the proportional SD. Section 2.2 mentions
  natural-log transformed concentrations, which the text ties to the plotting
  of the data; the error model is taken as proportional, as the Results state.
* **ECMO clearance printed as 0.48 L/h.** The printed estimates give 0.458 L/h
  (see the Table 3 check above); the model uses the Table 4 coefficient.
* **Reference weight.** The equations print `WT/median(WT)`; the 12.6 kg median
  is stated in the text and Table 1.
* **ECMO and infection category are subject-level.** The paper gives no
  within-subject timing for ECMO cannulation; diagnosis is the admission
  diagnosis.
* **Covariates not retained.** Surgery status (removed at backward elimination,
  Table 2) and eGFR (not significant) are not in the model.
* **Dosing regimen.** The paper does not report individual regimens; the
  15 mg/kg q6h, 1-h infusion regimen used here is illustrative.
* **No published NCA.** The paper reports no Cmax, AUC or half-life values, so
  there is no NCA comparison table; the checks above are against the paper's own
  Table 3 arithmetic and against closed forms.
